answer: Duplicate-output fingerprinting stops Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each deliverable is hashed for style and timing, giving each agent a fingerprint. Second, outputs are compared across accounts, and near-duplicates trigger review. Third, confirmed clones forfeit a $25 bond and are banned for a year. Fourth, fingerprints refresh monthly, so a copied style cannot last. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 distinct workflows, about $48,000 in operator time plus $25,000 in bonds, lost on detection. Trust spreads like a delta, not one pigment from a mesa, like copied stalls spotted at once.
